about: Powers the 🏷 Brand Lab tab: a real brand build-out plus packaging product lines that turn millions of spare bulk cards into products people actually want. Everything marked (est.) needs verifying before you print money on it.

brand.positioning: A collector-run treasure brand out of Colorado Springs: every pack, chest, and display is hand-pulled from a real collection — not pallet bulk — with honest odds and museum-grade presentation.

taglines: Every pack is a real pull.
From one collector's chest to yours.
Opened, sorted, treasured — never pallet bulk.
brand.voice: Honest collector-to-collector. Show the sorting, show the odds, show the room. No 'guaranteed hit' hype — transparency IS the brand.
logoPrompts: Minimal flat vector logo, a golden treasure chest with a single card silhouette rising from it, dark navy background, gold and cyan palette, no text, no existing characters
Vintage wax-seal style emblem, ornate chest keyhole motif, single-color gold on black, engraved line style, circular badge, original design
Modern geometric monogram combining a 'C' and a chest lid opening, flat design, gold gradient on deep navy, app-icon ready

ipSafety.title: Read me before printing anything
rules: Selling GENUINE cards you own is protected resale (first-sale doctrine) — singles, lots, and repacks of real cards are fine to sell.
Never print Pokémon/Nintendo artwork, characters, logos, or the word 'Pokémon' on your packaging, brand, or 3D prints you sell. Your brand must stand on its own art.
'Compatible with trading cards' / 'fits standard 63×88mm cards' is the safe way to describe accessories and prints.

Repacks: disclose exactly what buyers get (card count, odds basis, era mix). eBay and Whatnot both require repack transparency and can ban 'gambling-style' listings — check each venue's current policy before launch. (est.)
AI-generated art for YOUR packaging must be original — prompt for original creatures/motifs, never 'in the style of' or named characters.
Don't sell 3D prints of slabs or anything that could pass as grading-company gear; stands, frames, and chests of your own design are fine.

packagingLines.name: Era Vault Packs
packagingLines.what: 12 real cards from one era (WOTC / EX / DPPt / SWSH / SV), sleeved, in a branded tuck box with an era label and pull-date stamp.
packagingLines.uses: The mid-bulk mountain — commons/uncommons with era identity
packagingLines.standout: QR on the box opens a page showing the exact sorting session it came from — provenance nobody else offers.

packagingLines.name: The Mystery Chest
packagingLines.what: 3D-printed mini treasure chest (your own design from 3D Studio) holding 20 cards + one guaranteed $10+ card, odds sheet printed inside the lid.
packagingLines.uses: Bulk + one sweet-spot card per unit as the 'hit'
packagingLines.standout: The chest IS the product — buyers keep it as a display box. Reprintable in team colors for events.

packagingLines.name: Frame-Ready Sets
packagingLines.what: 9 thematically matched cards (an evolution line, a type rainbow) mounted in a 3×3 display frame with a printed nameplate.
packagingLines.standout: Sold as wall art to non-collectors — a market your competitors ignore. Etsy-friendly.

packagingLines.name: Party Chest Favors
packagingLines.what: 10-pack of kid-friendly cards in a small branded sleeve, sold in bundles of 8/12 for birthday parties.
packagingLines.uses: The deepest bulk — commons with cool art, zero market value
packagingLines.standout: Parents on FB Marketplace buy these repeatedly — subscription potential ('party box of the month').

packagingLines.name: Binder Starter Kits
packagingLines.what: A 4-pocket binder + 50 curated cards (one era or one type), a checklist, and a 'how to collect' card written by you.
packagingLines.uses: Mixed bulk with a few shinies to hook new collectors
packagingLines.standout: The on-ramp product — every kid you convert becomes a repeat singles buyer.

packagingLines.name: Slab & Stand Bundles
packagingLines.what: A graded card sold WITH a custom 3D-printed stand (STL from the 3D Studio tab) and a printed spec card of its pop report.
packagingLines.uses: Your graded inventory + the 3D print pipeline
packagingLines.standout: Raises perceived value of every slab; the stand carries your logo into buyers' display shelves.

artPipeline.title: Generating the brand's art (original, sellable)
steps: Lock one logo from the prompts above (⚙ Live key → generate in your AI tool of choice, or commission from the prompt)
Build a repeating 'treasure pattern' (chests, keys, compasses, gems — original motifs) for box wraps and sleeves
Export print files: tuck boxes and sleeves need 300 DPI CMYK with 3mm bleed (est.) — online box printers list dielines per size
Order a short sample run (25–50 boxes) before any bulk print
Version everything — put a tiny batch code on each box so you can trace which design sells

printCategories.vendorType: Your printer — STLs from the 3D Studio tab

standout.idea: Provenance QR — every product links to its real sorting session photo (shot in 📷 Scanner). Nobody in repacks does verifiable provenance.
Den tours — a 60-second video walk of your 3D Den room with the week's inventory on the shelves, posted before each live show.
Chest Night — a weekly live auction stream where one Mystery Chest on the shelf gets cracked at every $500 in sales.
Local card-shop consignment of Frame-Ready Sets and Party Chests — Colorado Springs shops take 20–30% but move volume (est.).
Publish your sell-through numbers monthly — radical transparency content nobody else posts, and it feeds the YouTube channel.

items: Pick the brand name + lock the logo
Sort bulk into era boxes while watching TV — 30 min/day
Sample run: 50 Era Vault boxes + 10 Mystery Chest prints
List first batch on eBay + FB; note sell-through per line
Double down on the best-selling line only
Consider LLC + resale license once revenue is steady (see Game Plan tab)
